confirmed.title: Emoji break apart on any animated or curved text (flags, skin tones, families)
confirmed.see: He types G'day 🇦🇺 or 👍🏽 on his iPhone and picks any Animate preset (Fade in, Pop, Typewriter, Wave…) or moves the Curve slider. The flag turns into two boxed letters (A U), the skin-toned thumb turns into a yellow thumb next to a separate brown square, and a family emoji turns into three separate people. This does not stop when the entrance finishes. It lasts for the whole life of the layer, in the preview and in the exported video.
confirmed.test: HUNT-a emoji break apart on animated or curved text — a flag becomes two boxed letters, a skin tone becomes a separate square. It fails with: emoji fall apart the moment a text is animated or curved … the Australian flag is 133px wide as plain text but 272px with Fade in (finished); the Australian flag is 133px wide flat but 306px on a Curve; a thumbs-up with a skin tone is 139px … but 289px …; a family emoji is 150px … but 432px … Controls pass: plain AB is the same width animated and still, one letter is the same width curved and flat, and this browser draws the flag narrower as one picture than as two letters.

verdict.reason:
This is a real bug. I re-ran the test in the worktree on port 8911 and it failed with the same numbers the hunter reported. The flag is 133px as plain text, 272px with Fade in and 306px on a Curve. The thumbs-up with a skin tone is 139 vs 289/304, and the family is 150 vs 432/437. The test's controls passed: plain AB and a single letter come out the same width.

I also rendered '🇦🇺 👍🏽 👨‍👩‍👧' through FM.renderScene at t=3s, after the entrance has finished, and looked at the picture. Plain text draws a flag, a skin-toned thumb and one family picture. With Fade in (By Character) and with Curve 90, the same text draws two dashed boxed letters A and U, a yellow thumb next to a separate brown square, and three separate faces. confirmed.title: The caption editor writes his words over a different caption after a caption is deleted or re-timed in its own Aa sheet
confirmed.see: On his phone he is typing caption 2. He opens Aa and taps ✕ to remove a stray caption 1, then taps ✓. Caption 3 (Charlie) now says the same thing as caption 2, and Charlie's words are gone. The same happens if he changes the Start or End time of the caption he is typing in the Aa sheet: his words land on another caption and that caption's words are lost. There is no warning.
confirmed.test: HUNT-a deleting or re-timing a caption in the text editor makes Done write his words over a DIFFERENT caption. It fails with: … he typed caption 2, deleted caption 1 from the Aa sheet and tapped ✓ — the captions are now [Bravo, edited | Bravo, edited] instead of [Bravo, edited | Charlie]: Done wrote his words over Charlie, and Charlie is gone; he typed caption 1, moved its Start to 5 s in the Aa sheet and tapped ✓ — the captions are now [Alpha, edited | Charlie | Alpha, edited] instead of [Bravo | Charlie | Alpha, edited] … The Aa, ✕ and ✓ presses are real finger taps.
confirmed.evidence: js/text-edit.js:47 `return cueList(layer())[active.cueIndex] || null;` holds the caption by its index in the list. js/text-edit.js:550 (onInput) and :558 (commit on Done) write `c.text = input.value` into whichever caption is at that index now. confirmed.see: On his PC he adds a text and types Hello world. With the text card still open he clicks the ↶ undo button to fix a typo. The whole text layer disappears and the card closes. When he clicks ↷, the layer comes back reading Text. Hello world is gone for good. On a layer that already existed, ↶ quietly undoes whatever he did before he started typing instead.

It fails with: on PC he added a text, typed Hello world and pressed ↶ with the card still open: one ↶ (mouse) took away the whole text layer he was typing into, and the editor closed with it; ↷ brought the layer back reading Text — the words he typed, Hello world, are gone for good. Severity is low. He loses one caption's place and has to press ‹ once, and no data is lost. The suggested fix is right: take the target caption object before dropEmptyCreated(), then find its new index with indexOf. I did not edit anything, and I stopped the server afterwards.

verdict.reason:
The test fails as reported (at 380: Spin Blur is added and the browser closes). But the failure depends on how the test driver fakes a finger, not on anything a real phone does.

I copied the worktree to my scratchpad and added a probe test there. It logs every event during the same hold on the Spin Blur tile through tests/_cdp.py. With a 650 ms hold and with a 1500 ms hold, no `contextmenu` event fired. The lift still became a full tap: mousedown, mouseup and click all landed on `.fxb-thumb.fxp-thumb` inside the Default row. Touches sent through CDP's `Input.dispatchTouchEvent` never register as a long press, however long they are held. So every "hold" in this test is really a slow tap, and Chrome hit-tests that tap where the finger lifts.

A real phone behaves differently:
- **Android Chrome:** a hold past the system long-press time (400–500 ms) is a long press. It fires `contextmenu`, which the app already blocks at js/fx-browser.js:336, and no click follows the release. The only exception would be a lift between 420 and 500 ms on phones running Android 11 or older, which is far too short a window for "every time".
- **iPhone (Safari/WebKit):** the test does not exercise WebKit at all. For a quick tap, WebKit only sends the click if the element under the finger is still the one that was pressed, and here it is not. Whether the click after a longer hold is re-aimed at whatever is under the finger now is something I cannot prove here: there is no iOS Simulator device on this Mac, and simctl hangs on the unaccepted Xcode licence.

So "with real touches … every time" overstates what was measured. The only input used was the CDP touch, and that input has no long-press step. Nothing in REQUESTS.md or POLISH-LOG.md records Ezra ever saying that holding an effect added it. He has browsed these preset sheets on his phone, and #407 is about the card inside one.

Open risk: I am not certain, but I recall that iPhone Safari may send the click after a hold to whatever is now under the finger. If so, this bug would be real on iPhone, and on more tiles than Spin Blur, because the preset rows under other tiles also add on click. One hold on Spin Blur on his phone settles it. The hunter's suggested fix, ignoring a click in the presets sheet unless the press started inside it, is cheap and harmless either way.

I did not change the worktree; the probe copy has been deleted and its server stopped. (By code reading only, unverified: on Android 12 and later, the `contextmenu` fires at about 400 ms and opens the presets. The 420 ms timer at js/fx-browser.js:325 does not check `_lpFired`, so it probably opens a second, stacked presets sheet.)

confirmed.test: HUNT-c a duplicated project is still called X copy after he opens it — it never turns into a second card with the original name. Only the index card gets `name` (the X copy text). After that, every save runs touchCurrent at js/storage.js:2198 `e.name = P.name || 'Untitled'`, which overwrites the card with the document's name. verdict.reason:
Confirmed as a real bug. I served the worktree on port 8913 and re-ran the test with ?only=HUNT-c a duplicated project, and it failed the same way the hunter reported: after duplicating, opening the copy and going back Home, the copy card reads "HUNTc Beach", 2 cards carry that name, and the editor also calls the copy HUNTc Beach.

Why it happens (read in the worktree's js/storage.js):
- duplicate() (line ~2330) passes the name "<card name> copy" to duplicateFrom.
- duplicateFrom (line ~2351) writes the copy's document as `project: JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(doc.project))`. So the stored project.name keeps the original's name, and only the index card gets the " copy" name.
- open() → FM.storage.load() puts that document's name into FM.scene.project. Nothing in open() or load() copies the card's name into the scene (the only exception is the fallback when the load fails).
- touchCurrent (line ~2198) runs `e.name = P.name || 'Untitled'` on every autosave, on open, and when Home opens. So the first save after opening the copy overwrites the card's " copy" name with the original's.

The test's setup matches what a real user does. The test names the project through FM.projects.create, which writes the name into both the card and the document. A real rename (line ~2485) also writes into both, so on a real device the original's document carries the same name. The test drove the ⋯ button, Duplicate and the copy card with real mouse clicks, not synthetic events, and needs nothing unusual: tap Duplicate, open the copy, go back Home.

This is not new. The pre-refactor duplicate (before 610d9904, v16.80) wrote the document the same way and set only the card's name, so the bug goes back a long way and is not a regression from the refactor. I found nothing in REQUESTS.md saying a copy should take back the original's name, and it goes against what "X copy" on the card promises.

Why it matters to him: once the copy has been opened, it and the original look the same on Home. That is a real risk of deleting or editing the wrong project. The bulk Duplicate and the collab callers of duplicateFrom (which pass names of their own) go through the same code, so they have the same problem.

confirmed.title: A project played through to the end gets a plain black Home card
confirmed.see: He plays a project to the end with Loop off, then goes Home. The card for the project he was just working on becomes a solid black picture and stays that way until something re-captures it. This happens every time he watches a project through and then leaves.
confirmed.test: HUNT-c a project he played through to the end still has a picture on its Home card, not a plain black one. Fails in both passes: he played HUNTc end through to the end and went Home — its card is now a plain black picture (brightest pixel 0 of 255; halfway through it was 255), because the card is taken at the playhead, 1.00 s, the instant after every clip has ended
confirmed.evidence: When playback ends without Loop, it parks at js/app.js:2191 `FM.time = P.duration;`. Home.open then calls captureThumbSoon, which runs js/home.js:408 `FM.projects.touchCurrent(true)` and makeThumb. At js/storage.js:1905 that draws `FM.renderScene(src.getContext('2d'), FM.scene, FM.time)`. FM.isLayerVisibleAt (js/scene.js:1100) is `t < start + duration`, so no clip is visible at t = duration and only the background is drawn. Element thumbnails already avoid this with pickThumbTime (queue 488); project cards do not.
confirmed.fix: In makeThumb, when FM.time is at or past the project end, render one frame before the end: `(FM.time >= P.duration - 1e-3) ? Math.max(0, P.duration - 1/(P.fps||30)) : FM.time`. A fuller fix would reuse pickThumbTime's best-visible-moment rule. I tried the one-frame-back version temporarily and the test passed in both passes, then I reverted it.

verdict.reason:
This is a real bug that Ezra would hit. I re-ran the test against the hunt2-c worktree (the server was already running on 8913 from that folder) and it failed the same way: brightest pixel 0 at the end, 255 halfway through.

How it happens:
- Loop is off by default (js/app.js:9 `FM.loop = false`), and a new project's background is black (js/scene.js:629).
- Project length always equals the end of the last clip (FM.autoFitDuration, js/app.js:777-790).
- So when an ordinary playback reaches the end, js/app.js:2191 sets `FM.time = P.duration`. A clip is only on screen before its end time, so at that instant no clip is visible.
- Going Home runs captureThumbSoon (js/home.js:408), then touchCurrent(true), then makeThumb. makeThumb (js/storage.js:1905) renders at the raw FM.time, so the card shows only the black background.
- The 12-second periodic capture in touchCurrent also uses makeThumb, so just sitting at the end in the editor blackens the card too.

The strongest point is that the card no longer matches the preview. The editor preview does NOT go black there: render() at js/app.js:102 renders through FM._endInstantTime (js/compositor.js:15482). That was added for queue 549, in Ezra's words: "when you go to the end of a layer you can't see it anymore… even if it wasn't the last thing it should still be visible when you're at the end of it". So at the end he sees the last picture in the editor, and the Home card shows black.

The app has already treated this same end-of-timeline gap as a bug in two other places:
- Queue 631 (FM.frameExportTime): his "I did save Frame as pnj on the last frame and I got a black image".
- Queue 488 (pickThumbTime) for element thumbnails.
Queue 915 clause 1 also says "NO PICTURE BEATS A BLACK ONE", and a black Home card was fixed as a high-severity bug in v16.77. Nothing in REQUESTS.md asks for a black card at the end.

The parts that could be test artefacts don't change the result:
- FM.play() and FM.home.open() are what the Play and Home buttons run, and playback stops at the end through the real tick.
- The pinThumbnail step is only a check that the picture works halfway through, and the pin is cleared before the real measurement.
- Dragging the playhead to the end also lands exactly on the end instant (see the queue 631 comment), so playing through isn't the only way to get there.

Suggested fix, slightly different from the hunter's: in makeThumb, render at `FM._endInstantTime(FM.scene, FM.time)` rather than stepping back one frame. That makes the card match the preview exactly. It only moves the time when nothing is showing at the playhead and a clip ends right there, so it leaves real mid-timeline gaps alone. The step back is only 1e-4 s, so a video layer stays on the frame it is already sitting on.

confirmed.title: Holding a Home card to enter Select and then sliding the same finger only ticks the card he held
confirmed.see: On his phone he holds a project, template or element card until Select comes on, then slides the same finger down over the cards below to tick a run, which is what the code says this gesture does. Only the card he held gets ticked. The browser treats the slide as a scroll and cancels his finger after its first move. To take a run he has to lift his finger and tap each card, or drag again.
confirmed.test: HUNT-c holding a project card until Select comes on, then sliding the same finger down, ticks every card it passes. Fails in both passes with a real finger at 380 (touch driven through tests/_cdp.py): he held HUNTc run 4 until Select came on and slid the same finger down over HUNTc run 3 and HUNTc run 2 — only 1 of those 3 cards are ticked. The browser cancelled his finger after 1 move(s): the card was still a scrollable card when the finger went down, so the slide was handed to scrolling, not to the select
confirmed.evidence: In select mode the cards get touch-action none (styles.css:4713 `body.hm-selecting .hm-card { touch-action: none; }`). A hold enters select mode from a timer that fires after the finger is already down (js/home.js ~1700-1720). The browser only reads touch-action at touchstart, so this gesture keeps touch-action auto. Nothing cancels the native pan: the pointermove preventDefault does not stop scrolling, and there is no non-passive touchmove handler. The first move therefore becomes a pan, and pointercancel reaches js/home.js:1765 `finish(); cancelPress(card);`, which ends the paint. The hold also calls render() at js/home.js:1706, which detaches the card under the finger. Its events then stop reaching the window, so window-level listeners cannot help.
confirmed.fix: Register a non-passive touchmove listener on each card in selectify, `if (paint && ev.cancelable) ev.preventDefault()`, so the slide after the hold can never become a scroll. It must be on the card itself, because the held node is detached by the render. I tried this temporarily and the test passed in both passes, then I reverted it.

verdict.reason:
This is a real defect in a gesture the app is built to support, not a test artefact.

1. **It reproduces.** I ran the hunter's test on port 8913 against the worktree. It fails with the same message: only 1 of 3 cards is ticked, and the browser cancelled the finger after 1 move.

2. **The test driver is not the cause.** In a scratch copy (scratchpad/skc, not the worktree), I added a control test. It turns Select on first with the header button, then does the same real-finger slide. That ticks all 3 cards, so tests/_cdp.py can paint a run whenever the card already had `touch-action: none` when the finger went down.

3. **The proposed fix works.** In the same scratch copy I added a non-passive `touchmove` listener on each card in selectify that calls `preventDefault` while `paint` is live. The hunter's test then passes. So the failure is exactly the missing scroll block.

**The code path matches the report:**
- `styles.css:4713` sets `body.hm-selecting .hm-card { touch-action: none; }`.
- On a hold, that class is only added by the 380 ms `holdTimer` in `js/home.js` selectify, after the finger is already down. Browsers (Chrome and iOS WebKit alike) fix touch-action at touchstart.
- The card's `pointermove` `preventDefault` does not stop a pan.
- The pull-to-slam `touchmove` guard on `.hm-scroll` never sees these events: the hold's `render()` detaches the card under the finger, so its touch events no longer bubble up to the list.
- The first slide therefore becomes a pan or overscroll. `pointercancel` then runs `finish()` (js/home.js, the `pointercancel` handler), which ends the paint with only the held card ticked.

**This is intended behaviour that fails, not an unreachable state.** The selectify comments describe "hold a card to enter Select and drag across to take a run". The hold path even arms auto-scroll specifically for hold-then-drag. The timeline's identical long-press-then-paint gesture already needed `window.addEventListener('touchmove', stopScroll, { passive: false })` (js/timeline.js ~1487/1565), with the comment "keep the browser from panning instead of painting". Home never got the equivalent.

**One caveat.** On Android Chrome, a hold longer than the long-press timeout may stop scrolling on its own, so there it could sometimes work. Ezra uses an iPhone, where a pan after a still hold still scrolls or bounces and fires `pointercancel`, as REQUESTS #132 notes for this same list. He would hit it.

all.title: A project played through to the end gets a plain black Home card
all.see: He plays a project to the end with Loop off, then goes Home. The card for the project he was just working on becomes a solid black picture and stays that way until something re-captures it. This happens every time he watches a project through and then leaves.
all.test: HUNT-c a project he played through to the end still has a picture on its Home card, not a plain black one. Fails in both passes: he played HUNTc end through to the end and went Home — its card is now a plain black picture (brightest pixel 0 of 255; halfway through it was 255), because the card is taken at the playhead, 1.00 s, the instant after every clip has ended
all.evidence: When playback ends without Loop, it parks at js/app.js:2191 `FM.time = P.duration;`. Home.open then calls captureThumbSoon, which runs js/home.js:408 `FM.projects.touchCurrent(true)` and makeThumb. At js/storage.js:1905 that draws `FM.renderScene(src.getContext('2d'), FM.scene, FM.time)`. FM.isLayerVisibleAt (js/scene.js:1100) is `t < start + duration`, so no clip is visible at t = duration and only the background is drawn. Element thumbnails already avoid this with pickThumbTime (queue 488); project cards do not.
all.fix: In makeThumb, when FM.time is at or past the project end, render one frame before the end: `(FM.time >= P.duration - 1e-3) ? Math.max(0, P.duration - 1/(P.fps||30)) : FM.time`. A fuller fix would reuse pickThumbTime's best-visible-moment rule. I tried the one-frame-back version temporarily and the test passed in both passes, then I reverted it.

verdict.reason:
This is a real bug that Ezra would hit. I re-ran the test against the hunt2-c worktree (the server was already running on 8913 from that folder) and it failed the same way: brightest pixel 0 at the end, 255 halfway through.

How it happens:
- Loop is off by default (js/app.js:9 `FM.loop = false`), and a new project's background is black (js/scene.js:629).
- Project length always equals the end of the last clip (FM.autoFitDuration, js/app.js:777-790).
- So when an ordinary playback reaches the end, js/app.js:2191 sets `FM.time = P.duration`. A clip is only on screen before its end time, so at that instant no clip is visible.
- Going Home runs captureThumbSoon (js/home.js:408), then touchCurrent(true), then makeThumb. makeThumb (js/storage.js:1905) renders at the raw FM.time, so the card shows only the black background.
- The 12-second periodic capture in touchCurrent also uses makeThumb, so just sitting at the end in the editor blackens the card too.

The strongest point is that the card no longer matches the preview. The editor preview does NOT go black there: render() at js/app.js:102 renders through FM._endInstantTime (js/compositor.js:15482). That was added for queue 549, in Ezra's words: "when you go to the end of a layer you can't see it anymore… even if it wasn't the last thing it should still be visible when you're at the end of it". So at the end he sees the last picture in the editor, and the Home card shows black.

The app has already treated this same end-of-timeline gap as a bug in two other places:
- Queue 631 (FM.frameExportTime): his "I did save Frame as pnj on the last frame and I got a black image".
- Queue 488 (pickThumbTime) for element thumbnails.
Queue 915 clause 1 also says "NO PICTURE BEATS A BLACK ONE", and a black Home card was fixed as a high-severity bug in v16.77. Nothing in REQUESTS.md asks for a black card at the end.

The parts that could be test artefacts don't change the result:
- FM.play() and FM.home.open() are what the Play and Home buttons run, and playback stops at the end through the real tick.
- The pinThumbnail step is only a check that the picture works halfway through, and the pin is cleared before the real measurement.
- Dragging the playhead to the end also lands exactly on the end instant (see the queue 631 comment), so playing through isn't the only way to get there.

Suggested fix, slightly different from the hunter's: in makeThumb, render at `FM._endInstantTime(FM.scene, FM.time)` rather than stepping back one frame. That makes the card match the preview exactly. It only moves the time when nothing is showing at the playhead and a clip ends right there, so it leaves real mid-timeline gaps alone. The step back is only 1e-4 s, so a video layer stays on the frame it is already sitting on.

all.title: Holding a Home card to enter Select and then sliding the same finger only ticks the card he held
all.see: On his phone he holds a project, template or element card until Select comes on, then slides the same finger down over the cards below to tick a run, which is what the code says this gesture does. Only the card he held gets ticked. The browser treats the slide as a scroll and cancels his finger after its first move. To take a run he has to lift his finger and tap each card, or drag again.
all.test: HUNT-c holding a project card until Select comes on, then sliding the same finger down, ticks every card it passes. Fails in both passes with a real finger at 380 (touch driven through tests/_cdp.py): he held HUNTc run 4 until Select came on and slid the same finger down over HUNTc run 3 and HUNTc run 2 — only 1 of those 3 cards are ticked. The browser cancelled his finger after 1 move(s): the card was still a scrollable card when the finger went down, so the slide was handed to scrolling, not to the select
all.evidence: In select mode the cards get touch-action none (styles.css:4713 `body.hm-selecting .hm-card { touch-action: none; }`). A hold enters select mode from a timer that fires after the finger is already down (js/home.js ~1700-1720). The browser only reads touch-action at touchstart, so this gesture keeps touch-action auto. Nothing cancels the native pan: the pointermove preventDefault does not stop scrolling, and there is no non-passive touchmove handler. The first move therefore becomes a pan, and pointercancel reaches js/home.js:1765 `finish(); cancelPress(card);`, which ends the paint. The hold also calls render() at js/home.js:1706, which detaches the card under the finger. Its events then stop reaching the window, so window-level listeners cannot help.
all.fix: Register a non-passive touchmove listener on each card in selectify, `if (paint && ev.cancelable) ev.preventDefault()`, so the slide after the hold can never become a scroll. It must be on the card itself, because the held node is detached by the render. I tried this temporarily and the test passed in both passes, then I reverted it.

verdict.reason:
This is a real defect in a gesture the app is built to support, not a test artefact.

1. **It reproduces.** I ran the hunter's test on port 8913 against the worktree. It fails with the same message: only 1 of 3 cards is ticked, and the browser cancelled the finger after 1 move.

2. **The test driver is not the cause.** In a scratch copy (scratchpad/skc, not the worktree), I added a control test. It turns Select on first with the header button, then does the same real-finger slide. That ticks all 3 cards, so tests/_cdp.py can paint a run whenever the card already had `touch-action: none` when the finger went down.

3. **The proposed fix works.** In the same scratch copy I added a non-passive `touchmove` listener on each card in selectify that calls `preventDefault` while `paint` is live. The hunter's test then passes. So the failure is exactly the missing scroll block.

**The code path matches the report:**
- `styles.css:4713` sets `body.hm-selecting .hm-card { touch-action: none; }`.
- On a hold, that class is only added by the 380 ms `holdTimer` in `js/home.js` selectify, after the finger is already down. Browsers (Chrome and iOS WebKit alike) fix touch-action at touchstart.
- The card's `pointermove` `preventDefault` does not stop a pan.
- The pull-to-slam `touchmove` guard on `.hm-scroll` never sees these events: the hold's `render()` detaches the card under the finger, so its touch events no longer bubble up to the list.
- The first slide therefore becomes a pan or overscroll. `pointercancel` then runs `finish()` (js/home.js, the `pointercancel` handler), which ends the paint with only the held card ticked.

**This is intended behaviour that fails, not an unreachable state.** The selectify comments describe "hold a card to enter Select and drag across to take a run". The hold path even arms auto-scroll specifically for hold-then-drag. The timeline's identical long-press-then-paint gesture already needed `window.addEventListener('touchmove', stopScroll, { passive: false })` (js/timeline.js ~1487/1565), with the comment "keep the browser from panning instead of painting". Home never got the equivalent.

**One caveat.** On Android Chrome, a hold longer than the long-press timeout may stop scrolling on its own, so there it could sometimes work. Ezra uses an iPhone, where a pan after a still hold still scrolls or bounces and fires `pointercancel`, as REQUESTS #132 notes for this same list. He would hit it.

I did not edit the worktree.

confirmed.title: A 30 fps clip exported at 30 fps drops every third frame and shows the one before it twice
confirmed.see: Any ordinary 30 fps phone clip judders in the exported MP4 (and in GIF and PNG frames), even though the preview plays it smoothly. I decoded every frame of the file: it reads 0,1,1,3,4,4,6,7,7 and so on. Source frames 2, 5, 8 and so on never appear, and the frame before each one plays twice. That is 28 of 90 frames. At 60 fps the same fault hits a different third of the frames.
confirmed.test: HUNT-d a 30 fps clip exported at 30 fps drops every third frame and shows the one before it twice — fails with: 28 of the 90 frames in the exported MP4 show the wrong moment of the clip (frame 2 shows 1, frame 5 shows 4, frame 8 shows 7 …), and source frames 2, 5, 8, 11, 14, 17, 23, 26 … are not in the file at all — every third frame of a plain 30 fps clip is dropped and the one before it plays twice, so the export judders where the preview plays smoothly.
confirmed.evidence: js/exporter.js:177 `const target = Math.min(Math.max(time, 0), …)` seeks each video to exactly t = start + f/fps (run() frame loop), which lands exactly on a source-frame boundary. The clip's frames start at k/30, which the browser stores in whole microseconds (33333, 66667, 100000 …). The seek to 2/30 is stored as 66666 µs, 1 µs before frame 2, so it lands on frame 1. A probe of the bare element confirmed it: currentTime = k/30 lands on 0,1,1,3,4,4,6,7,7. Control in the test: the fixture decodes as 0..89 in order. A throwaway fix (target + 0.5 ms) turned this test green and was reverted. The frame cache (js/frames.js buildFrameCache seeks i*dur/count) has the same boundary problem for reversed clips.
confirmed.fix: Seek slightly inside the frame instead of onto its boundary, for example target + about 0.5 ms (well under one frame at any real rate). Apply the same change to buildFrameCache's seekAndPaint targets so reversed and frame-blend clips are fixed too.

verdict.reason:
This is a real defect, at least in Chrome. I re-ran the test against the worktree on port 8914 and it failed exactly as reported: 28 of the 90 exported frames are wrong, and the file reads 0,1,1,3,4,4,6,7,7,9,10,10,12,13,13. The control passes, so the fixture clip decodes as 0..89 in order and the demuxer, decoder and bar reader are sound.

I then checked the claimed cause on a bare video element, outside the app, in the preview browser (Chromium 152):
- Seeking to exactly k/30 for k=1..14 showed frames [1,1,3,4,4,6,7,7,9,10,10,12,13,13].
- Seeking to k/30 + 0.5 ms showed [1..14], all correct.
- Seeking to mid-frame, (k+0.5)/30, also showed [1..14].

So the cause is the seek landing exactly on a frame boundary, not the exporter's compositing or the test harness. Per the hunter's explanation (the 0.5 ms nudge fixing it agrees): the browser stores frame 2 at 66667 µs (2/30 rounded to the nearest microsecond), while the seek target 2/30 lands at 66666 µs, one microsecond short, so frame 1 shows.

Code path: js/exporter.js run() sets t = start + f / fps (lines 1258/1267). seekAllVideos then calls seekVideo, which sets el.currentTime = target (line 177) with no offset. For a forward clip with no frame-blend, the compositor draws straight from the element (js/compositor.js ~14744 only uses the frame cache for reversed or frame-blend clips).

The fixture is not a special case. Its timestamps sit on the exact k/30 grid, which is what a real iPhone 30 fps clip has (20/600 steps). The trigger is the most ordinary export there is: an imported clip at start 0, untrimmed, in the default 30 fps project, exported at 30 fps. The result is a 10 Hz stutter that is visible on any pan.

Nothing in REQUESTS.md says exact-boundary seeking is intended, and there is no user-state or synthetic-event artefact. Two limits:
- It is proven only in Chromium. His iPhone's Safari/AVFoundation may round the seek time differently, so I cannot confirm it there. It does hit his PC/Chrome exports.
- The frame-cache (reversed clip) part of the claim was not checked.

verdict.reason:

verdict.reason:
This is a real bug. I ran the test on its own at 380px against the served worktree and it failed the way the report says: X at 1.5 s was 200.0 both before and after, and the diamond showed as eased (ease-smooth, green).

The code matches the report:
- **What the menu writes:** the diamond menu's Ease and Hold items write to that diamond's own keyframe (js/timeline.js:2684 and 2692).
- **What playback reads:** FM.evalProp works out a segment's easing only from `b`, the keyframe the segment ends on. The `ez`, `bez`, `e` and hold checks at js/scene.js:91-105 all read `b`. Nothing ever reads the easing on kf[0]: before the first keyframe, evalProp returns kf[0].v, and a looping animation wraps back into the keyframe range, so there is no segment that ends on kf[0].
- **The graph editor agrees with playback, not the menu:** pickKfs in js/graph-editor.js edits the end keyframe of the segment the playhead is in.

So the menu on the first diamond writes an ease that nothing reads, while the diamond recolours to say it is eased.

It is not an artefact of the test:
- The input is real, not synthetic. A still hold opens the menu, and a tap on Ease In-Out does change the keyframe; the test checks both before its main assertion.
- The state is easy to reach: a two-keyframe A-to-B move, with Move mode and Transform open, which is how anyone edits one.
- Ezra has never said easing should go only on the keyframe a move arrives at. I searched REQUESTS.md and found nothing on which keyframe an ease belongs to.

The codebase itself shows the confusion. The shipped effect presets in js/fx-presets.js put the ease on the FIRST keyframe, e.g. Beat Slam `{t:0, e:'easeOut'}, {t:0.45, e:'linear'}`. Because evalProp reads the end keyframe, that ease is dead too and the preset plays linear. This is a related side finding the hunter did not report.

On a phone, the hold menu is the main way into easing: a finger never double-clicks or right-clicks. He has an even chance of holding the start diamond of a move, and when he does the control does nothing and the green colour says it worked. With three keyframes the menu also eases the wrong segment: holding the middle one changes the move INTO it, not out of it.

The report slightly overstates one thing: the graph editor is also reachable on a phone, so the menu is not strictly the only way to ease a keyframe. The defect stands regardless, and medium severity is fair.

confirmed.fix: Stop the Set from growing. verdict.reason:
This is a real problem. I re-ran the test on the unmodified worktree and it failed the same way: after 6 tries on the Filters tab and 5 opens of the effects browser, 384 of the 413 thumbnails that were on screen were still in memory after a forced garbage collection. That is 56.6 MB of picture memory, plus 3,515 page elements and 1,281 listeners more than before.

The cause is in js/fx-thumbs.js. `mountKey` adds every tile canvas to the module-level Set `mounted` (line 1597). The only code that ever removes anything from that Set is inside `remountLive()` (line 1701). The only thing that calls `remountLive()` is `photosChanged()` (line 112), which runs when the fx-art photos finish decoding. `preloadArt` is guarded by a `preloaded` flag, so that happens about once a session. After that nothing ever gives the canvases back.

Each canvas also keeps its whole removed panel alive. `inspector.refresh()` clears the panel with `root.innerHTML = ''`, and its own comment says it "rebuilds the whole panel on EVERY edit". So while the Filters tab is showing, every rebuild adds 56 more tiles at 192x192 (about 8 MB), and the old panel is kept along with them. That happens on opening the tab, Add, Undo, a slider drag, or the playhead crossing a clip edge. The effects browser and the Presets card add to the same Set.

To check that the Set really is what holds them, I copied the worktree to the scratchpad and changed one thing: `mountKey` now drops disconnected canvases that are not waiting in `pendingQ`. With only that change, the same test passed. So the Set is the cause, not the test's own setup.

Checks against it being a test artefact:
- The test drives the same functions the real buttons call (the Filters button calls `openCategory('filters')`; `FM.fxBrowser.open` and `close`).
- The leak does not depend on synthetic pointer events or timing.
- `document.createElement` is only wrapped with WeakRefs, which cannot keep anything alive.
- Nothing in REQUESTS.md asks for this behaviour, and the code's own comment in `remountLive` says the Set must not "grow forever".

Why it matters on his phone: iOS Safari has a limit on total canvas memory. Growing by about 8 MB per Filters rebuild can reach it in one session of trying looks. When it does, the tab can reload and lose unsaved edits, or the canvases stop drawing.

Two small corrections to the report:
- "Every Filters build" is really every inspector rebuild while the Filters tab is showing, which happens more often than the report suggests.
- `pendingQ` can also keep a few detached canvases whose tiles never painted, until `stopAll` runs. That is minor next to the Set.

I did not edit the worktree. The scratch copy has been deleted and both test servers are stopped.

verdict.reason:
I re-ran the test alone on port 8916 and it fails the way the hunter said. After the heavy stretch the tier is 3 (48%). It is still 3 after 1800 frames at 10 ms, which is 60% of a 60 fps frame.

The code matches the claim. In js/app.js, `_playTier` (line 141) is only ever written by notePlaybackCost. FM.play (around line 2250) resets `_renderAvg`, `_tierCooldown` and `_dropFrom`, but not the tier or `_locked`. Nothing in project open or storage touches it; I grepped js/projects.js and js/storage.js and found nothing. A tier only climbs when the cost is under 30% of the frame budget (line 350), and nothing ever tests whether the tier above would be affordable. The payoff test (line 338) only judges drops made in the current scene. So a tier earned in a heavy project carries into a light one and is never checked again.

The key point is that the same scene gives a different result depending on history:
- **Fresh session:** a scene costing 10 ms never passes the 72% drop line (12 ms), so it plays at 100%.
- **After a heavy stretch:** the same scene plays at 48% until reload.

This goes against the setting's own promise in settings.js ("Auto measures your machine and uses as much detail as it can hold"). It also goes against the ladder's purpose in its own comments, which quote Ezra: "its having to lower the quality when i do something as simple as just have one simple video". Treating render time as mostly unaffected by resolution is the app's own measured model (12.2 ms to 8.3 ms for 13x fewer pixels), not something the test made up. A real person reaches this state by working in a heavy project, then removing the effects or opening a plain project without reloading. His samples show 60 fps projects, where the stuck band is 5 to 12 ms of render time. That is a realistic cost for a plain video; his PC measured 12.59 ms. Nothing in REQUESTS.md or the code asks for the tier to persist.

The report overclaims in three places:
1. **The #657 sample:** it does not prove this. Its 12.59 ms at 28% is above the drop line, so history dependence cannot be told apart from ordinary ladder behaviour there.
2. **"For the rest of the session, in every project":** too strong. The tier is shared with the drag path, so a scrub whose render costs under 5 ms, or any playback under 30% of budget, still climbs back. It only stays stuck for scenes whose cost sits between the two lines, which at 30 fps is 10 to 24 ms.
3. **What he sees:** only playback and drags are soft. A paused frame is always full resolution.
